data.body:
# "Checks that don't check" — a taxonomy, from eight proven instances in one session

2026-09-05 overnight. Every entry below was PROVEN by experiment or measurement, not inferred.
Recorded because the instances share structure, and the structure predicts where to look next.

## The shared shape

A guard exists, runs, and reports success — while the property it was built to protect is false.
It fails SILENTLY, and it fails in the direction of reassurance. In every case the guard's own
output was the reason nobody looked closer.

## The instances

1. **Clamp destroys the signal.** `pct_of_cap` clamped to 100, so five cap-compliance metrics
   could never report an overshoot. A cap-compliance metric that cannot say "over cap" is not a
   check. (Fixed, change 2679.)

2. **Ancestry test wrong for the merge strategy.** `git merge-base --is-ancestor <pushed-sha>
   origin/main` reports NOT-MERGED for a change Gerrit rebased on submit. Reproduced live:
   `feature/s1-windows-sweep-probe` labelled `ABANDONED?` while its Change-Id is in main.
   (`felicific-blueribbon-kitty`.)

3. **Flag consulted after the early return.** `force_new_store` was INERT on the linked-worktree
   path: `init.py` returned via `_init_via_symlink` before the flag was read, so a caller
   demanding an isolated store silently got the live one. This is the duplicate-ticket root cause.
   The first fix — a warning — was refuted by the class-level RED test, which still failed.
   (`anarchic-princely-raven`.)

4. **Missing data votes as a breach.** `treat_missing_data = breaching` with
   `datapoints_to_alarm < evaluation_periods` lets absent buckets out-vote a real healthy
   datapoint. Confirmed live at 20:47Z: four alarms fired simultaneously with every StateReason
   naming missing-data, while Gerrit answered HTTP 200 in 0.27 s and root disk read 71-76% against
   an 85% threshold. (Change 2683.)

5. **Bounds that never sum.** `observability.sh` held OVER 495 s of individually-defensible
   ceilings inside a 240 s `TimeoutStartSec`. Each carried a comment justifying itself against the
   total; nothing added them up. The journal section reasons "12 x 10s = 120s < 240s" while the
   docker section was separately entitled to the same 240 s. Two `du` walks over the same ~1.88M
   file tree at 120 s each = exactly 240 s. (Change 2684.)

6. **Detection computed, then discarded.** `create_ticket` already returns a `duplicate_warning`
   on a same-normalized-title collision (`_lib_writes.py:182`) and would have fired on all 425
   duplicates. `_warn_advisory` hands it to the caller and nothing aggregates, counts, or alarms.
   The detector existed; the *listener* did not. (`prenatal-maudlin-seahorse`.)

7. **The write that appears issued and never lands.** MCP `comment_ticket` / `create_ticket`
   exceeding the client deadline return a timeout while the write does not land. Three agents hit
   it independently; all fell back to the CLI, which completed the identical writes instantly. One
   agent could not file the bug it had just found, because filing it hit the bug.
   (`lousy-unsuited-gnu`.)

8. **Coverage assumed, not proven.** Nine error counters were to be moved to `notBreaching`,
   with dead-man duty implicitly delegated to "the heartbeats". Measurement showed the early
   heartbeats present in 54 buckets where a counter was absent — they demonstrably do NOT stop
   together. Real coverage came from a TAIL sentinel, and the residual fell monotonically to zero
   with proximity to it (3,3,3,3,2,1,0,0). Now build-enforced. (Change 2683.)

## What generalises

- **A guard that cannot express failure is not a guard.** (1), (6). Ask of any check: what is the
  observation that makes it say NO, and can that observation occur?
- **Absence is not evidence.** (4), (7), (8). Silence gets read as health. Every dead-man needs a
  positive liveness signal, not an inference from quiet.
- **Local justification does not compose.** (5). Each ceiling was correct in isolation. Correctness
  of parts is not correctness of the whole, and nothing in review catches a sum.
- **The test must match the mechanism, not the intent.** (2). `is-ancestor` is a correct ancestry
  test; it is the wrong question under rebase-on-submit.
- **Order of evaluation is a silent contract.** (3), (8). A flag read after an early return, and a
  publish order that carries a dead-man, are both invisible until violated.

## Method notes that earned their keep

- **A test whose PASS is also what the failure mode predicts is worthless.** Two of my own
  analyses were withdrawn for this: binding-distinctness (the map is keyed by ticket id, so a
  re-create overwrites and an orphan is invisible) and per-title Jira-vs-rebar count match (an
  inbound echo creates one on EACH side and preserves the match). Both "passed"; neither could
  have failed.
- **Isolated timings mislead; in-situ traces do not.** The probe RCA measured `du` standalone and
  nearly shipped a "halve the walk" fix. Interleaving the probe's own breadcrumbs with the unit
  lifecycle across ten killed runs showed a single walk does not complete at 95 s or 125 s either.
- **Perturb the fix.** Two agents found holes in their own tests this way — one discovered that
  deleting its entire new helper left every behavioural test green, because the portability stub
  discarded the value under test.
- **Make load-bearing order enforceable.** Where an invariant lives in ordering, a test that fails
  on reordering converts a convention into a property.

## Where to look next

Any check whose success path is "nothing was observed". Any bound justified against a total that
something else is also spending. Any flag read after a branch that can return early. Any advisory
value returned to a caller with no aggregator. Any ancestry/identity test written before the
merge strategy it now runs under.
